label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition-Potsdam
current definition: The German centre of the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, a cohort of 27,548 adults from the general population around Potsdam in eastern Germany, mostly aged 35–65 at recruitment in 1994–1998, followed up prospectively to study diet, metabolism and chronic diseases such as type 2 diabetes and cancer.

problems: The definition calls EPIC-Potsdam 'The German centre' of EPIC, but EPIC has two German centres. The cohort's own institute says: 'There are two study centres in Germany: the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) supervises the EPIC-Heidelberg cohort and the DIfE is participating in the cohort with the EPIC-Potsdam Study.' The cancer aim was only inferred from the EPIC name (review note: 'cancer implied by the EPIC name'). The same page supports it ('EPIC was developed to examine the relationships between diet, nutritional status, lifestyle and environmental factors, as well as the incidence of cancer and other chronic diseases lilke type 2 diabetes'). It also gives the recruitment, which the definition lacks (random draw from the population registers of Potsdam and the surrounding area, 1994-1998), and the exact ages (women 35-64, men 40-64), which the definition rounds to 'mostly aged 35–65'. 27,548 and 1994-1998 are right (PMID:23043162). current definition: A multicentre community-based cohort of about 16,000 men and women aged 18–74 who self-identify as Hispanic or Latino, recruited from random samples of households in the Bronx, Chicago, Miami and San Diego in the United States, to study the prevalence of and risk factors for cardiovascular, pulmonary, metabolic and other chronic diseases.

label: China Medical University Hospital Biobank
current definition: A hospital-based cohort of about 413,000 patients of China Medical University Hospital and its affiliated branches in Taichung, Taiwan, genotyped on a custom Taiwan Precision Medicine array and linked to electronic medical records from 2003 to 2021 (the HiGenome resource), assembled for genome-wide, phenome-wide and polygenic risk score studies in the Taiwanese Han population.
proposed definition: A hospital-based cohort of patients of China Medical University Hospital, an academic medical centre in Taichung, Taiwan, and its affiliated hospitals, recruited through the hospital's Precision Medicine Project, begun in 2018 to collect biospecimens from patients attending for medical visits, from densely populated towns and districts across Taiwan. About 413,000 participants enrolled from 2018 to 2021 were genotyped on the custom Taiwan Precision Medicine (TPMv1) array and linked to their electronic medical records from 2003 to 2021 (the HiGenome resource; 323,397 passed ancestry and quality control), for genome-wide, phenome-wide and polygenic risk score studies in the Taiwanese Han population.
problems: The definition puts the whole cohort in Taichung ('China Medical University Hospital and its affiliated branches in Taichung'), but the source says CMUH, in Taichung, 'collaborates with a network of hospitals across the northern, central, and southern regions of the country' and that 'patients were enrolled from highly populated towns and districts across Taiwan from 2018 to 2021'; the recruitment route and years (the CMUH Precision Medicine Project, 'initiated in 2018 to recruit subjects and collect biospecimens from all patients who come to CMUH for medical visits', PMID:36769103; enrolment 2018–2021) and the number passing QC (323,397 of 413,000) are missing. The rest is right (custom TPMv1 array, EMRs 2003–2021, GWAS/PheWAS/PRS aims, Taiwanese Han). Missing names used by the cohort's own papers: 'China Medical University Hospital (CMUH) Precision Medicine Project' (PMID:36769103) and 'Precision Medicine Project (CMUHPMP)' (PMID:37752970). No parent: the TPMI cohort paper (PMID:41092961) treats CMUH as a separate cohort ('In addition to the TPMI, TWB and China Medical University Hospital (CMUH) represent two additional large cohorts for genetic studies in Taiwan'), so no isSubCohortOf TPMI (COHO:0000622); it gives CMUH 170,000 participants, as does PMID:36769103 ('More than 170,000 subjects have been enrolled to date', 2023), against HiGenome's 413,000 (2025). Synonym missing: the PGS Catalog other name 'MAYO clinic biobank' differs from the label only in capitalisation and must be kept (capitalisation rule); it is also what ties the PGS id MAYO to this term. label: HOLBAEK Study
current definition: A cohort of Danish children and adolescents combining an obesity clinic cohort treated at the Children's Obesity Clinic, Copenhagen University Hospital Holbæk, and a population-based cohort recruited from schools in 11 municipalities in Zealand, enrolled between 2009 and 2019 with genotyping and deep cardiometabolic phenotyping to study the causes and consequences of childhood obesity.

label: FinnGen
current definition: A public–private partnership research project in Finland that combines genotype data from newly collected and legacy samples of about 500,000 participants of a nationwide network of Finnish biobanks with digital health data from national health registers, to provide genetic insights into disease in an isolated population enriched for low-frequency variants.
problems: Definition, label, acronyms (FINNGEN, Finngen; FinnGen is the label itself), synonyms, country and example are right; no duplicate (the other Finnish terms, e.g. COHO:0000070, 0000071, 0000420, 0000435, 0000496, 0000891, are different cohorts). The cited profile (Kurki et al. 2023, data release 5) gives 500,000 only as the target ('FinnGen aims to study the genome and national health register data of 500,000 Finnish individuals.'; 224,737 analysed), so 'about 500,000 participants' needs the project's website, which now says it 'has collected and analysed genome and health data from 500,000 Finnish biobank donors'. Type: kept as cohort, but the sources leave it open: FinnGen is one study with one protocol, genotyping, imputation and register linkage, analysed as a single sample ('the FinnGen cohort'), yet its participants were not recruited under a common protocol ('Samples have not specifically been collected for FinnGen, but the study has incorporated all that have been available in the biobanks'; about 200,000 legacy samples from earlier research cohorts and 300,000 prospective samples from Finnish biobanks). COHO types comparable umbrellas (KORA, FINRISK, National Biobank of Korea) as aggregations but hospital biobanks (BioVU, Mass General Brigham Biobank) as cohorts; curator may decide. label: PainOMICS Retrospective Study
current definition: A retrospective, multicentre case–control study of adults with chronic low back pain and controls, recruited at clinical pain centres in Italy, Croatia, Belgium, Australia and the United States within the European Union FP7-funded PainOMICS project, collecting clinical data and blood samples for genome-wide association, glycomics and activomics analyses of chronic low back pain.
proposed definition: A retrospective, multicentre case–control study of adults of Caucasian ancestry with chronic low back pain and controls without chronic pain, run within the European Union FP7-funded PainOMICS project (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02037789), which enrolled 3,400 participants between September 2014 and February 2016 at clinical centres in Italy, Belgium, the United Kingdom and Croatia (the registered protocol also listed sites in the United States and Australia), collecting clinical data and blood samples for genome-wide association, glycomics and activomics analyses of chronic low back pain.
problems: Identity, label, type, acronyms and example are right: the only Painomics-tagged paper (PMID:40593539, 255 studies) uses this study, and its Supplementary Note describes it as the retrospective multicentre study NCT02037789 of the FP7 PainOmics project. The definition and the countries follow the protocol's project-level sentence 'The project includes six clinical centres from Italy, Croatia, Belgium, Australia and the USA' (PMID:27798002), which covers all four PainOMICS trials. The sources on the sample actually recruited give different countries. The SOP paper's Table 1 lists King's College London (UK) among the centres enrolling patients (PMID:28459826). The 2025 GWAS supplement says the study was approved by the review boards of 'all clinical centers (King’s College London, ZOL Genk/Lanaken, St. Catherine Specialty Hospital) that enrolled patients' after San Matteo Pavia, and that 3,400 were enrolled between September 2014 and February 2016. label: Diabetes Heart Study
current definition: A family-based cohort of European American and African American siblings concordant for type 2 diabetes, and their unaffected relatives, recruited from internal medicine and endocrinology clinics in western North Carolina, United States, to study genetic and epidemiological contributions to diabetic heart disease and subclinical cardiovascular disease.
proposed definition: A community-based, family-based study of European American and African American siblings concordant for type 2 diabetes and their unaffected relatives (1,443 participants from 564 families), recruited from internal medicine and endocrinology clinics in western North Carolina, United States, and examined at Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center to study genetic and epidemiological contributions to diabetic heart disease and subclinical cardiovascular disease; a parallel African American-Diabetes Heart Study (AA-DHS) later enrolled unrelated African Americans with type 2 diabetes to study ethnic differences in calcified atherosclerotic plaque.
problems: Right cohort (the Wake Forest Diabetes Heart Study), label, type and country; no duplicate. The term's GWAS tags and example cover the DHS family, not only the family-based DHS that the definition describes. The example GCST90244653 is tagged AA-DHS. Its paper names the TOPMed sample 'Diabetes Heart Study (DHS, n = 365)' with dbGaP phs001412, which dbGaP titles 'NHLBI TOPMed: Diabetes Heart Study (DHS) African American Coronary Artery Calcification (AA CAC)'. The same TOPMed sample is tagged DHS in PMID:40216759 ('DHS (AA CAC)', n = 384, Supplementary Data). The DHS investigators call the African American-DHS 'a second, parallel study' (PMID:21409311) that 'started after DHS and enrolled unrelated AAs', and its analysis sets add the DHS African Americans (PMID:29221444). So there are two options. Either this term covers both, and then it must carry the tag AA-DHS (the rules require every GWAS tag used for it) and the definition must mention AA-DHS (proposed here). Or AA-DHS is minted separately, and the example moves to the DiabHS-tagged GCST90278455 (CAC GWAS PMID:37770635), whose supplementary study table lists 'DHS | Diabetes Heart Study | European Ancestry', 1115 participants, Wake Forest. The term is in no subset, although GWAS Catalog tags denote it (DiabHS on GCST90278455/6, DHS on GCST90502911/3/4, AA-DHS on four studies of PMID:36220816) and its example is a GCST: it should be in the GWAS subset. The definition also leaves out the size (1,443 participants from 564 families, PMID:21409311). Namesakes: the tag DHS on GCST012442 (PMID:34108613) is the deCODE health study (COHO:0000468, note present). The PGS cohort DHS (named 'Dortmund Health Study') is used for this study in the TOPMed evaluations of PGS005093/PGS005094 (PMID:41888514: 'Diabetes Heart Study[DHS]'), and for Dortmund in PGS000767.
